issues.description: Trainer config keys are accessed inconsistently — max_step required, save_interval/log_interval required, val_interval missing entirely
issues.detail: The docstring promises max_steps, log_interval, val_interval, save_interval, but the code reads max_step (singular), save_interval, log_interval, and never reads val_interval. log_interval is read but never used. The contract between config-as-value and trainer-as-behavior is complected and unverified. Specify the config shape as data, validate it once at construction, fail loudly on mismatch.

issues.description: valid() accumulates Python lists of per-batch means and averages them, conflating per-batch and per-sample statistics
issues.detail: Each batch's stat is already a mean across the batch (after all_reduce/world_size). Averaging those means across batches of unequal size produces a wrong dataset-level number. The value 'validation loss' and the identity 'per-batch reduction' are complected. Carry (sum, count) values explicitly, or weight by batch size.

issues.description: Checkpoint selection sorts by lexical split of directory name without validating the parse — incidental complexity around place-oriented filenames
issues.detail: step_ is used as both a marker and a delimiter; any name containing 'step_' qualifies, and the int() parse will crash on malformed names. The 'latest checkpoint' identity is being inferred from filesystem places rather than from a value (a log/manifest). A small checkpoints.json log of (step, path) would make time and identity explicit.

issues.description: train() advances global_step inside the data loop but the outer run() loop checks max_step only between save_intervals — overshoots and never logs validation at the boundary
issues.detail: run() calls train() (which runs save_interval steps), then valid(), then saves, then re-checks the while condition. global_step can exceed max_step by up to save_interval-1, and validation only runs on save_interval boundaries. The time semantics of 'when do I stop' and 'when do I validate' are complected with 'when do I checkpoint'. Separate the three schedules.

issues.description: wandb is treated as ambient global state and made mandatory — identity and behavior of logging are complected with the trainer
issues.detail: The trainer reads/writes a module-level wandb.run and wandb.config, and the docstring says 'wandb is MANDATORY.' This is place-oriented programming: the logger is a place, not a value. Pass a logger object (or a no-op logger) into the trainer. Then 'mandatory wandb' becomes a choice at the call site, not a hidden coupling.

issues.description: Specifier strings parsed by string.split() everywhere — the 'specifier' value has no schema, just a stringly-typed contract
issues.detail: 'task:name:data_json[:factor]' is a value pretending to be a string. It is split twice (once by whitespace, once by ':') in scattered places. Define a Specifier dataclass or NamedTuple parsed once in argparse, and pass values around. Easy to keep as strings; not simple.

review.summary: The PR builds a DeepSpeed training launcher and trainer that work, but several concerns are complected and several values are stringly-typed or place-oriented. The trainer_args dict has no schema and is accessed by inconsistent keys (max_step vs max_steps, val_interval declared but unread). Validation statistics conflate per-batch and per-sample means. Checkpoint identity is inferred from filesystem names rather than a manifest, and stop/validate/save schedules share one counter inside an inner loop. wandb is treated as ambient global mandatory state rather than a value passed in. None of this is hard to fix; most of it would shrink if config and specifiers were parsed once into typed values and logging were dependency-injected.
